narrator.text: It's 7:02 a.m. Your alarm goes off, so you smack the snooze button.
narrator.design: A warm, confident male storyteller in his thirties with a slightly mischievous, playful tone, like a YouTube story narrator. Emotion: playful and knowing, a little smile in the voice, as if you know something is about to go wrong.

you.text: Okay, so this is going to sound completely ridiculous, but I promise you every single word of it is true.
you.design: A young man in his early twenties with a light, expressive voice. Emotion: animated, storytelling to a friend.

roommate.text: Okay, so this is going to sound completely ridiculous, but I promise you every single word of it is true.
roommate.design: A young woman in her twenties with a bright, energetic voice. Emotion: animated, storytelling to a friend.

theo.text: Okay, okay, hear me out, this next bit is actually funny, I tested it on my mom and she almost smiled.
theo.design: A young man in his mid twenties, the narrator's best friend: warm, slightly nasal, eager and a bit nervous, an aspiring stand-up comedian. Emotion: hopeful, animated.

man.text: Honestly, I have no idea what's going on today, but everyone I talk to is acting completely different.
man.design: A man in his thirties with a plain, friendly, everyday American voice. Emotion: casual, slightly confused.

woman2.text: Honestly, I have no idea what's going on today, but everyone I talk to is acting completely different.
woman2.design: A woman in her forties with a crisp, professional, slightly tired voice, like an office manager. Emotion: matter-of-fact.

older.text: Honestly, I have no idea what's going on today, but everyone I talk to is acting completely different.
older.design: An older man in his late fifties with a deep, gravelly, gruff voice. Emotion: blunt, world-weary.

grandpa.text: Now listen, kiddo. When I was your age, we didn't have any of this, and we turned out just fine, mostly.
grandpa.design: A warm, gentle American grandfather in his late seventies, slightly raspy and soft, kind and a little playful. Emotion: tender.

grandma.text: Oh, sweetheart, come in, come in. I just made coffee, and you look like you haven't slept a wink.
grandma.design: A warm American grandmother in her mid seventies, soft and slightly shaky, loving, with quiet humour. Emotion: gentle, a little tired.

mom.text: Oh, come on, you two. Dinner's getting cold, and I am not reheating it again. I mean it this time.
mom.design: A warm, witty American mom in her late forties with a bright, expressive voice, quick dry humour and a lot of love in it. Emotion: playful, affectionate.

dad.text: Alright, alright, I'm coming. Has anyone seen my keys? They were right here, I swear, two seconds ago.
dad.design: A goofy, warm American dad in his late forties with a friendly, slightly husky voice, always half-joking. Emotion: cheerful, easygoing.

max.text: Nobody ever asks what my power is. That's fine. I don't need anyone to ask. I just need everyone to listen.
max.design: A seventeen year old boy with a quiet, flat, slightly nasal voice, calm and a little unsettling, speaking slowly and clearly. Emotion: calm, detached.
